chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding

A man has some wealth of orphans with one of his family members, so he hands it over to him. He takes from it dirhams which he needs, and the one who had the wealth of the orphans does not know that he has taken anything from their wealth. Then he becomes affluent after that. Which is better for him: to give it to the one in whose hand it was, or to hand it over to the orphan who has reached maturity? And would it suffice if he hands it over to his companion as a gift and does not inform him that he had taken some wealth of his?

He (peace be upon him) said: Whichever of those he does will suffice for him, when he delivers it to its owner. For this is from the secrets (of the guardian's intention). If it is from his intention to return it to the orphan, if he has reached maturity, in whichever manner he wishes, even if he does not inform him that he had taken something for him; and if he wishes, he can return it to the one in whose hand it was.
And he (peace be upon him) said: If the owner of the wealth is absent, let him hand it over to the one in whose hand it was.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a guardian takes from an orphan's wealth without their knowledge and later repays it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling in the context of *al-sarā'ir* (secrecy), where the guardian may discreetly repay the orphan's wealth to the custodian rather than the orphan directly, provided the intention is to settle the debt. This flexibility highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the guardian's sincere intent (*niyyah*) and practical necessity over rigid formalism, ensuring the orphan's asset is preserved without the need for explicit notification. The ruling underscores the trustworthiness required of guardians managing *mal al-yatīm* (orphan's wealth) under the broader Quranic mandate of careful stewardship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> regarding

the man a family member of his happens to have some wealth of the orphan, so he handed it over to him. So he took some Dirhams from it which he was needy to, and the one who had the wealth of the orphan did not know that he has taken anything from the wealth of the orphan. Then he became affluent after that. Which is better for him, giving it to the one in whose hand it was or hand it over to the orphan, and he (the orphan) has reached maturity? And would it suffice if he was to hand it over to his companions upon a relevant aspect (as a gift) and not let him know that he had taken some wealth of his?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever of that he does would suffice for him, when he delivers it to his companion, for this is from the secrecies when it was from his intention to return it to the orphan, if he had attained maturity, upon whichever aspects he so desires to, even if he does not let him know of it that he had grabbed something of his; and if he so desires to he can return it to the one in whose hand it (originally) was’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the owner of the wealth was absent, so let him hand it over to the one in whose hand it (originally) was’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about

the case of a man in whose family someone has the assets of orphans and he gives a certain amount of dirham to him that he needs; and the person with whom there are the assets of orphans does not know if he has taken anything from their assets. He thereafter becomes affluent. Is it better for him to give it back to the one who had given him such assets or to the orphan who has reached maturity? Is it sufficient if he gives it to the one from whom he had received the amount in the form of gifts without informing him about his borrowing anything from him?

He (the Imam) said, ’Either way is sufficient. To give it as gift to his friend is sufficient because it is of the secret matters, if he had the intention to return to the orphan who has become mature, and in whatever manners he returns even if he does not inform him about his borrowing or if he wants he can return to the one from whom he had received the amount.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If his friend is absent, he then must return it to the one from whom he had received the amount.’”
